deck.title: Elastic Beanstalk
deck.analogy: Elastic Beanstalk is a fully furnished apartment: you bring your suitcase (code), everything is set up, and you still get the keys to every room.

cards.front: What is Elastic Beanstalk's core idea?

back.answer: You upload code; Beanstalk provisions EC2, an Auto Scaling Group, a Load Balancer and CloudWatch monitoring for you.
back.explanation: You don't configure them but can see and tune all of them.
back.mnemonic: Fully furnished apartment, and you still get the keys to every room.

cards.front: Which languages/platforms does Elastic Beanstalk support?

back.answer: Java, Python, Node.js, .NET, Go, Ruby, PHP, or Docker.

cards.front: Is Elastic Beanstalk a black box? What control do you keep?

back.answer: No. It's an orchestrator; you retain full control of the underlying resources.
back.explanation: Identity phrase: deploy a web app quickly without managing infrastructure BUT retain control over resources.

cards.front: How is Elastic Beanstalk priced?

back.answer: Beanstalk itself is free; you pay only for the resources it creates (EC2, ALB, etc.).

cards.front: What is .ebextensions in Elastic Beanstalk?

back.answer: YAML/JSON config files in your code bundle that customize the environment (packages, env vars, resources).

cards.front: What is an Elastic Beanstalk Worker environment?

back.answer: A tier that pulls jobs from an SQS queue instead of serving web traffic; the background-processing tier.

cards.front: Beanstalk All at once deployment: downtime, capacity, cost, rollback, when to pick?

back.answer: Downtime YES; capacity drops to zero briefly; no extra cost; rollback by slow redeploy. Fastest; dev/test.

cards.front: Beanstalk Rolling deployment: downtime, capacity, cost, rollback, when to pick?

back.answer: No downtime; reduced capacity (a batch is always down); no extra cost; slow rollback. Pick for no downtime + no extra cost.

cards.front: Beanstalk Rolling with additional batch: downtime, capacity, cost, rollback, when to pick?

back.answer: No downtime; full capacity maintained; small extra cost (one batch); slow rollback. Pick when reduced capacity is unacceptable.
back.explanation: Spins up one extra batch first, then rolls.

cards.front: Beanstalk Immutable deployment: downtime, capacity, cost, rollback, when to pick?

back.answer: No downtime; full capacity; briefly double cost; safest rollback (delete new fleet). Pick for production, safest rollback.
back.explanation: Builds a whole new fleet alongside the old, swaps when healthy.

cards.front: Beanstalk Blue/Green deployment: downtime, capacity, cost, rollback, when to pick?

back.answer: No downtime; full capacity; double cost while both exist; instant rollback by swapping CNAME back. Test on a real URL, instant switch.
back.explanation: Clones the entire environment, tests it, then swaps DNS CNAMEs.

cards.front: Beanstalk Rolling vs Rolling with additional batch: what's the difference?

back.answer: Rolling reduces capacity at no extra cost; with additional batch keeps full capacity for a small extra cost.
back.explanation: The extra batch covers the gap while others update.

cards.front: Beanstalk Immutable vs Blue/Green: what is swapped and how is rollback done?

back.answer: Immutable builds a new fleet in the same environment; rollback deletes it. Blue/Green clones the whole environment; rollback swaps the CNAME back.

cards.front: Beanstalk: what happens to an RDS database created inside the environment when the environment is terminated?

back.answer: The database dies with the environment; its lifecycle is tied to it.
back.explanation: Production rule: create RDS OUTSIDE the environment and pass the connection string via environment variables.

cards.front: How do you migrate an RDS database out of an existing Beanstalk environment?

back.answer: Snapshot the RDS instance, restore as standalone RDS, point the environment at it via env vars, enable deletion protection.

cards.front: Question wants fine-grained, repeatable infrastructure as code: Beanstalk or what?
Question wants microservices at scale / container orchestration: Beanstalk or what?
Question wants event-driven, sub-15-minute functions: Beanstalk or what?
What is Elastic Beanstalk the right fit for?

back.answer: One classic web app, developers who want speed, with control retained.

cards.front: Developers want to deploy code quickly without managing infrastructure but must retain full control of the underlying resources. Which service?

back.explanation: That is its identity phrase verbatim.

choices.why: Serverless; not about retaining control of resources.
Quick deploy while keeping control of resources.
IaC templates, not quick code deploy.

cards.front: Deploy a new Beanstalk version as fast as possible; brief downtime is acceptable (dev environment). Which policy?

back.explanation: Speed plus downtime-OK is the only reason to pick it.

choices.why: Slower; builds a whole new fleet.
Batches are slower than updating all at once.

cards.front: Deploy a Beanstalk update with no downtime and no additional cost. Which policy?

back.explanation: Batches reuse existing instances; capacity dips but nothing new is billed.

choices.why: Reuses existing instances; no new billing.

cards.front: Deploy a Beanstalk update with no downtime while maintaining full capacity. Which policy?

back.explanation: The extra batch covers the capacity gap.

choices.why: Possible, but the pattern targets the extra batch.

cards.front: Beanstalk deployment must be safest possible with quick rollback if health checks fail. Which policy?

back.explanation: Bad deploy? Delete the new fleet; the old one is untouched.

choices.why: New fleet deleted on failure; old untouched.
Rollback is slow, batch by batch.

cards.front: Test the new Beanstalk version on a separate URL, then switch all traffic instantly with instant rollback. Which approach?

back.explanation: DNS swap works in both directions.

choices.why: No separate URL to test; same environment.
Separate environment; swap CNAMEs both ways.

cards.front: A Beanstalk app's database was lost when the environment was terminated. How to prevent this in production?

back.answer: Create RDS outside the environment; connect via environment variables.

choices.text: Enable Multi-AZ on the embedded RDS
choices.why: Doesn't stop deletion with the environment.

choices.text: Create RDS outside the environment; use env vars
choices.why: Decouples DB lifecycle from the environment.

cards.front: Migrate a database out of an existing Beanstalk environment. What do you do?

back.answer: Snapshot the RDS instance, restore as standalone RDS, then reconnect via env vars.

choices.text: Snapshot RDS and restore as standalone RDS
choices.why: Creates an independent DB to reconnect via env vars.

cards.front: Long-running background jobs from a queue alongside a Beanstalk web app. Which feature?
Customize packages and configuration of Beanstalk instances at deploy time. Which mechanism?

back.explanation: Config files in the source bundle.

choices.why: Config files in the bundle customize instances.
